correctness.rationale: The kernel has exactly p^r-1 nonidentity elements, all of order p, so its psi-value is D=p^(r+1)-p+1. For every nontrivial complement element c^j, fixed-point-freeness makes c^j-1 invertible, while the q-term geometric sum annihilates c^j-1; hence that sum operator is zero and every element outside the kernel has order q. This gives psi(G)=D+p^r q(q-1). The complement acts semiregularly on V\{0}, so q divides p^r-1. Therefore D is congruent to 1 modulo both p and q, giving gcd(D,psi(G))=gcd(D,q-1). Since q<=p^r-1, this gcd is strictly smaller than D. The packaged replay reconstructs several scalar and nonscalar actions and verifies the full element-order distribution.

value.rationale: The existence of a nonabelian psi-divisible group is explicitly open in the inspected literature. Frobenius groups with elementary abelian kernels and prime complements form a natural infinite class of nonabelian solvable groups, including standard affine examples such as A4. The theorem rules out the entire noncyclic-kernel family with one intrinsic subgroup witness and an exact gcd formula, extending beyond the cyclic-Sylow/ZM obstructions already known. This is a structural elimination of a motivated candidate family, not a finite census or isolated example.
